title: Randomized controlled trial on the prevention of postoperative dry eye following cataract surgery
summary:
Cataract surgery is a very common and generally safe procedure. Nevertheless, some patients report symptoms such as a burning sensation, a feeling of a foreign body in the eye, dryness, or blurred vision after surgery. These symptoms can affect patient satisfaction following the procedure.
This study aims to investigate whether moisturizing eye drops, when used regularly before surgery, can reduce such symptoms after surgery. The research question is: Does preventive treatment with moisturizing eye drops prior to cataract surgery help prevent or alleviate symptoms of dry eye after surgery?
The study includes patients scheduled for cataract surgery. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group will use preservative-free moisturizing eye drops five times a day for three weeks prior to surgery. The other group will not use any additional moisturizing eye drops before surgery. The surgery and standard post-operative care will be the same for both groups.
As part of the standard pre- and post-operative examinations, symptoms are recorded using questionnaires and the lubrication of the eyes is assessed. These examinations take place before the surgery, on the day of the surgery, on the first day after the surgery, after 1 week, after 4 weeks, and after 3 months. Participation is voluntary and may be discontinued at any time without providing a reason.

interventions.name: Intervention group – Standardized preoperative lubrication therapy using preservative-free artificial tears containing 0.24% hyaluronic acid and glycerin, e.g., Artelac® Complete MDO®. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients may be enrolled in the study if all of the following criteria are met:
1. Planned elective cataract surgery, on an outpatient or inpatient basis, at the Department of Ophthalmology at TUM Klinikum rechts der Isar.
2. Age between 18 and 100 years at the time of study enrollment.
3. Ocular surface / dry eye status of the study eye:
  - Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI) < 33 or OSDI-6 <9
  - Schirmer I test > 5 mm
  - Tear Break-Up Time (TBUT) > 7 seconds
4. No use of lubricating eye drops or other artificial tears within the last 4 weeks prior to study enrollment.
5. Ability to understand the nature, significance, and implications of the study and to provide written informed consent.
6. Sufficient knowledge of German or English to understand the patient information, complete questionnaires, and reliably follow examination instructions, e.g., regarding fixation during imaging or vision testing.
7. Ability and willingness to reliably adhere to the prescribed instillation schedule. In cases of limited ability to self-administer, enrollment is only possible if regular use is ensured by a suitable caregiver.
8. Enrollment regardless of gender.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients must not be included in the study if any of the following criteria apply:
1. Active diseases of the ocular surface or eyelids that may influence the study endpoints, in particular: active blepharitis, active conjunctivitis, keratitis, ocular infection, significant eyelid malposition, or lagophthalmos.
2. Systemic diseases that may be associated with a clinically relevant disorder of the ocular surface or tear film function, in particular: Sjögren’s syndrome, other relevant autoimmune diseases with ocular involvement, severe atopic or mucocutaneous diseases involving the ocular surface.
3. Pre-existing significant sicca syndrome meeting at least one of the following criteria: 
 - OSDI ≥ 33 or OSDI6 ≥ 9
 - Schirmer I test ≤ 5 mm
 - TBUT ≤ 7 seconds
4. Current use of contact lenses or contact lens use within the 4 weeks prior to study enrollment.
5. Use of topical eye drops within the 4 weeks prior to study enrollment that may affect the ocular surface or tear film parameters, in particular: lubricating eye drops/tear substitutes, topical immunosuppressants (e.g., cyclosporine or tacrolimus), topical steroids, topical nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, antiallergic eye drops, other regular local ophthalmic therapy, provided it may influence the study endpoints.
6. Pre-existing ocular conditions or prior surgeries that may significantly affect the assessment of the ocular surface or postoperative endpoints, in particular: previous refractive corneal surgery, corneal transplantation, relevant corneal scarring or corneal dystrophies, recurrent corneal erosions, punctum plugs, or the condition following surgical punctal occlusion.
7. Planned combined intraocular procedures or anticipated complex cataract surgeries, provided that these may result in significant deviations in the postoperative ocular surface or the postoperative treatment regimen.
8. Known hypersensitivity or intolerance to components of the study medication or to diagnostic substances used during the study, as applicable.
9. Cognitive, psychiatric, neurological, or other impairments that significantly interfere with the ability to make independent decisions, reliably participate in the study, complete the questionnaires, or adhere to the eye drop regimen.
10. Other medical or organizational reasons for which the investigator deems participation in the study inappropriate.
